text: The file name is the version of record, so the source is version 2 and this document is version 3; the internal stamp of 1 is kept as a source fact and named in the metadata table.
why: The file name and the folder holding it say v2, while the metadata table says Version 1 and no other copy exists.
read: Recovery Workbench Personal Data Protection Design v2.docx, title block and metadata table
applied_in: Title block; metadata table row Source version
impact: Document control only; no business value changes.

text: Every personal data category, table and control is assigned to the service that owns the table in Ownership Map v1, with the service and schema taken from Architecture v5 slide 41.
why: Version 2 names roles and monolith tables only; the realignment needs a service owner for each PII boundary.
read: Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 to 20 and 41; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
impact: Sets the per-service boundary used by the service stories and the data stories.

text: The consent state is held in rwb_source_data.contact_point_ext, owner P1; the column is cited in this design by the version 2 name contact_point.consent_status until the P1 design fixes the target column name.
why: The target table is known from the Ownership Map but the target column name is not in any source.
read: Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet (contact_point_ext, owner P1); v2 section 3
applied_in: Section 3 closing paragraph; section 11 table row P1
impact: The consent read path in the P1 and P6 stories; no change to the R-UNI-10 rule.

text: This version is issued as Draft because no approval or document status is recorded in version 2.
why: The D-RCV-60 overlay issues unapproved documents as Draft and records the assumption instead of stopping.
impact: None on content; the approval step follows after the run.

text: For a debt sale, S6 rwb-debtsale selects the fields to the sale terms and P2 rwb-integration performs the masking check when it delivers the encrypted file; the per-sale field list comes from the sale terms.
why: Version 2 requires a masking check but names neither the selecting service nor the checking service, and the field list is sale-specific.
read: v2 sections 4 and 8; Architecture v5 slide 19 (rwb-debtsale lots and data room, rwb-integration buyer file INT-25); Ownership Map v1
applied_in: Section 4 closing paragraph; section 8 closing paragraph; section 12 files
impact: The S6 and P2 stories carry the check; no new control is added.

text: The read log of a personal field is the ACE Common PII Kafka path to the SOC for all 19 services; Recovery adds no business topic and no second audit path for it, and the field-level event contract stays with the ACE team.
why: The sources give the PII logging path but no Recovery-owned event contract, and Architecture v5 keeps business topics separate from PII logging.
read: v2 section 5; Architecture v5 slides 8, 22 and 34
impact: No new topic, no new story for a Recovery read log.

text: A data subject request is served by reading each owning service's contract under the Compliance role and scope, joined on the case ID from rwb-case; no new retrieval service is added.
why: Version 2 fixes the 30-day path through Compliance but the sources define no cross-service retrieval flow.
read: v2 section 7; Architecture v5 slides 14 to 20 and 41; Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet
impact: Compliance and P3 procedure only; no schema change.

text: The national ID and passport token is minted by rwb-source-data (P1) at load and no clear value is written to any schema; the token format and any detokenization path are fixed in the P1 design and in the P4 access profile.
why: Version 2 says the value is tokenized at load but not who mints the token or in what format, and P1 is the only service that reads the ACE views.
read: v2 section 4; Architecture v5 slides 7 and 15; Ownership Map v1 (extension tables, owner P1)
impact: The P1 load story and the P4 masking profile; no change to the minimization rule.
